title: Harn Museum of Art opens a landmark exhibition of contemporary Cuban art by women
summary: The Harn Museum of Art at the University of Florida will present more than 60 works by 10 Cuban women artists in the landmark exhibition Layered Lives opening Aug. 25, 2026. Originating from the Discoveries in Art Certilman Family Collection, the exhibition brings together three decades of photography, paintings, ceramics and prints illustrating the resilience, innovation and expansive creativity of Cuban women artists whose layered stories continue to shape our understanding of Cuba and its diaspora. The exhibition will be on view through Jan. 3, 2027. Layered Lives features work by artists Belkis Ayón, Ariamna Contino, Aimée García, Rocío García, Alejandra Glez, Elsa Mora, Mabel Poblet, Sandra Ramos, Adislen Reyes and Linet Sánchez. The works can be approached in diverse ways as they contain many interconnected stories and meanings. title: National Gallery acquires notable historical and contemporary works
summary: The National Gallery of Art today announced the acquisition of significant new works, marking a meaningful expansion of the nation’s art collection. The acquisitions, spanning rare examples of devotional art, historical paintings, contemporary print multiples, and a noteworthy photography collection, showcase major artistic movements and innovative uses of materials across centuries. Notable among the additions to the collection are a suite of woodblock prints by T.C. Cannon; a 17th-century crucifix painting by María Josefa Sánchez; a major work by Wifredo Lam, completed after his return to Cuba in the early 1940s; and a painting by Christina Quarles, one of the only finished works in her Altadena studio to survive the 2025 Eaton Fire in Southern California. title: Einstein letter and early Marilyn Monroe release feature in rare autographs auction
summary: An Albert Einstein autograph letter written in German, signed and sent from Berlin, Germany in 1926; a Marilyn Monroe early 1946 “Photographic Model Release” signed as “Norma Jean Dougherty” when she was just 19; and a monumental World War II map boldly signed by Winston Churchill are a few of the highlight lots in University Archives’ online-only Rare Autographs, Manuscripts, Books & Photographs auction set for Wednesday, September 9. The auction, starting promptly at 10am Eastern Time, is filled with items in many categories. The catalog in its entirety – all 409 lots – is up for viewing and bidding now on the University Archives website, www.UniversityArchives.com , plus the popular platforms Invaluable.com, Auctionzip.com and LiveAuctioneers.com. title: Hauser & Wirth New York presents first solo exhibition with Lee Bul
summary: This September, Hauser & Wirth New York will present the gallery’s first exhibition with Lee Bul, one of the most influential artists of her generation and a singular voice in contemporary art’s ongoing reckoning with the promises and failures of modernity. Bringing together major new sculptures with recent bodies of work, ‘The Anatomy of Every Setting Sun,’ organized by guest curator Dr. Jiyoon Lee, extends Lee’s decades-long examination of humanity’s drive to transcend nature through technology and systems of control. The works on view reveal the tensions between utopian aspiration and inevitable collapse, exposing the entangled relationships between technology, history and nature. This presentation comes at a pivotal moment for the artist, ahead of the opening of ‘Lee Bul: From 1998 to Now,’ her major traveling survey exhibition at the Museum of Contemporary Art Antwerp,

title: Lagos Biennial presents inaugural Curatorial Lab Lagos led by Adam Szymczyk
summary: The Lagos Biennial is pleased to announce the inaugural Curatorial Lab Lagos—an intensive three-day programme led by Adam Szymczyk. Taking place immediately after the Biennial's opening weekend, Curatorial Lab Lagos is conceived as an experimental platform to question inherited exhibition models and to imagine new curatorial futures from Africa and beyond. This idea first manifested during the 2019 edition of the Lagos Biennial as a curatorial intensive programme. Responding to the Biennial's 2026 theme, The Museum of Things Unseen, the programme invites participants to rethink the museum, the exhibition, and the canon itself. Through collective discussion, site visits, presentations, and workshops, participants will investigate how curatorial practice can become a tool for rewriting institutional histories, challenging dominant narratives, and inventing new forms of cultural imagination. Rather than teaching established methods, the Curatorial Lab asks a more urgent question: How

title: Gagosian to participate in Frieze Seoul with solo presentation of works by Damien Hirst
summary: Gagosian announced its participation in Frieze Seoul with a selection of paintings and sculptures by Damien Hirst, drawn from many of the artist’s most acclaimed series. The presentation follows Hirst’s celebrated exhibition at the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Seoul, his first museum retrospective in Asia, which attracted more than half a million visitors. Over the past four decades, Hirst has probed the boundaries of art and life, confronting the forces that shape human experience through a range of forms, materials, and strategies. The ultimate provocateur, he has turned to both the shocking and the seemingly banal to explore the intersections and complexities of beauty, belief, and truth. title: Explore the making of one of Australia's greatest artists in Nolan: Origins
summary: A visionary artist and cultural icon, Sidney Nolan transformed the image of a nation and changed the course of Australian art with his depictions of the country’s landscapes and legends. Opening at the Art Gallery of New South Wales in October, the major exhibition Nolan: Origins, journeys through the artist’s formative years and the extraordinary body of work that established him as a defining figure in modern art. Spanning the remarkable creative period from the late 1930s until Nolan’s departure for the United Kingdom in 1953, and bringing together more than 150 significant works from public and private collections, Nolan: Origins is the first major survey dedicated exclusively to the artist’s early years in Australia. The exhibition traces the intense output of a young artist who achieved artistic maturity with remarkable speed,

title: Joe Diggs and Whitney Hagen bring two distinct visions of abstraction to Venice
summary: Two American painters with very different approaches to abstraction will take over neighboring spaces at Castello 925 this fall, offering visitors a pair of exhibitions that move between memory, color, geometry and the physical experience of painting. Opening during the same week and running from September 24 through November 22, 2026, Joe Diggs: In Venice and Whitney Hagen: Chromatic Conditions form part of Castello 925's program alongside the 61st Venice Biennale. Both exhibitions respond, in their own ways, to the Biennale's theme, In Minor Keys. An opening reception for the shows is scheduled for Saturday, September 26. The similarities largely end there. For Joe Diggs, abstraction emerges from memory, family history and the textures of everyday life. title: Brutus Art Space to host Santiago Sierra's largest Netherlands solo exhibition
summary: From 20 September to 20 December 2026, Brutus Art Space presents DEATH & MONEY by Santiago Sierra, the largest solo exhibition of the artist's work ever presented in the Netherlands. Curated by A/POLITICAL, the exhibition brings together existing and newly commissioned works that expose the ongoing geopolitical entanglement of war and profit. Brutus director Sanne ten Brink: "Santiago Sierra creates work that challenges, provokes and sparks debate. That is precisely why we believe it is important to show his work. With DEATH & MONEY, he poses an uncomfortable yet urgent question: how do we relate to war, violence and injustice when we are confronted with them on a daily basis?" Santiago Sierra's work examines the mechanisms of labour, inequality, state power and economic exploitation. title: David Kordansky Gallery presents Tala Madani solo exhibition Control X
summary: David Kordansky Gallery announced Control X, an exhibition of new paintings and video animations by Tala Madani. The exhibition is on view in Los Angeles at 5130 W. Edgewood Pl. from September 18 through October 24, 2026. Control X features several new bodies of paintings and new animations in which characters and settings subject themselves, willingly or not, to forces by which they are broken down and reformed. The works address mythologies of creation as they trace the fine lines between making and destroying in art, language, history, and human relationships. By foregrounding acts of markmaking, the exhibition establishes emotionally resonant parallels between the worlds the figures inhabit and the materially present world of painting itself. The result is a form of realism that goes beyond artifice, and that allows the work to address the widest possible range of historical, art historical, and contemporary crises with both humor and critique. title: Mixed-media artist Farhad Ostovani to visit the Nelson-Atkins
summary: Mixed-media artist Farhad Ostovani will visit The Nelson Atkins Museum of Art this October for a discussion on an exhibition of his work now on display at the museum. This special event explores the intersection of sight and sound in Farhad Ostovani: Goldberg Variations. Inspired by Johann Sebastian Bach’s beloved keyboard composition, Ostovani’s series on the Goldberg Variations depicts plant forms—the flowerless stems and leaves of rose plants— which move and twist across empty space. Working with ink and brush, impressions, and chalk lines, he builds up his compositions from delicate layers of Nepalese paper. These botanical forms are his invented symbolic language for depicting the auditory experience of music. “Farhad Ostovani is an artist of great sensitivity,” said Julián Zugazagoitia, Director & CEO of the Nelson-Atkins. “He has the ability to strip his subject down to its bare essence.

title: Rare first edition, first printing Harry Potter hardback comes to auction
summary: Nate D. Sanders Auctions is set to auction the most coveted book in the Harry Potter canon: a first edition, first printing hardback of J.K. Rowling's debut novel, "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone." This particular copy is one of only 500 hardback editions from the initial printing, making it far scarcer and more collectible than the softcover edition published concurrently. Shortly after its debut in June 1997, the novel soared to the top of book lists voted on by children, prompting adults across the publishing world to take notice. The phenomenon of Harry Potter only grew stronger over the following years, as more Millennial children aged into reading the book and its sequels, famously devouring each new installment the day it was released. title: Frist Art Museum announces 2027 schedule of exhibitions
summary: The Frist Art Museum announced its 2027 schedule of exhibitions. In the Ingram Gallery, the year begins with The Great Mughals: Art, Architecture, and Opulence, a major exhibition showcasing the dazzling art and vibrant culture of the Mughal court’s golden age, which brought together cultural elements from South Asia, Iran, China, and Europe. Concurrently on view, French Impressionism and the Nabis: Works from the Collection of Marlene and Spencer Hays features a cross section of works by artists such as Edgar Degas, Eva Gonzalès, Henri Matisse, Berthe Morisot, Odilon Redon, and Édouard Vuillard from the legendary Nashville collection. In the summer, Pop to Present: American Art from the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts traces the diversity and creativity of artists working in the United States from the 1940s to the present through celebrated figures ranging from Jackson Pollock and Andy Warhol

title: PICA closes 2026 program with a major SPACED collaboration and landmark Shannon Lyons mid-career survey
summary: Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts will open the final season of its 2026 artistic program this October with Circular Economies, a major exhibition presented in partnership with SPACED that brings the outcomes of socially-engaged artist residencies across regional Western Australia into PICA’s Central Galleries. Running from 17 October to 20 December 2026, this season brings together local, national and international perspectives through three distinct presentations: Circular Economies in the Central Galleries; Cafe coming soon, a major mid-career survey exhibition by Western Australian artist Shannon Lyons in the West End Gallery; and Foragers in PICA’s Screen Space presented by Palestinian artist Jumana

title: Albumen Gallery announces representation of photographers Naomi Lewis & Maria Daniel Balcazar
summary: Naomi Lewis and Maria Daniel Balcazar are two outstanding photography artists whose respective body of works – in subject matter as well as technique and style - are testament to the breadth and richness of contemporary photography. Albumen’s Director and Founder, Stephan Schmid said, “We are pleased to announce the representation of two formidable artists in the international fine art photography world – Naomi Lewis and Maria Daniel Balcazar. In their own respective subject matters and artistic style the works of Naomi Lewis and Maria Daniel Balcazar align perfectly with Albumen Gallery’s commitment to championing boundary-pushing photographic art. title: Heritage Auctions names Scott Dicken West Coast Consignment Director of Animation and Anime
summary: Heritage Auctions has named longtime animation art specialist Scott Dicken Consignment Director of Animation & Anime Art. Based in Heritage’s Beverly Hills office, Dicken brings more than 34 years of industry experience to the world’s leading auction house for animation art. Dicken joins Heritage after more than three decades with Chuck Jones Galleries, where he rose from Art Sales Consultant to Vice President of Sales. During his tenure, Dicken helped expand the gallery business, develop new locations and cultivate lasting relationships with collectors, artists and animation-industry professionals across the country. “Scott has been a respected presence in the animation art community for decades, and we’ve known and worked with him for years,” says Jim Lentz, Heritage Auctions’ Vice President and Director of Animation & Anime Art. “He

title: ACC presents Space-Out Competition with visual artist Woopsyang
summary: Every day, we are surrounded by screens, sounds, and endless streams of information. In a world of constant connection and immediate response, simply pausing has become an extraordinary experience. As the first program in the ACC Future Class series, ACC presents Space-Out Competition at ACC Hanul Madang, a participatory performance with visual artist Woopsyang. Through this project, the artist invites participants to space out together. For 90 minutes, participants will do nothing—gradually becoming aware of their bodies, their breathing, and the world around them. Space-Out Competition at ACC Hanul Madang transforms the ordinary act of resting into a shared artistic experience. title: O-Overgaden announces autumn exhibition lineup featuring emerging international artists
summary: O—Overgaden is one of the few large-scale art institutions in Denmark with an unwavering focus on mounting exhibitions by emerging artists, local and international. This autumn, alongside IN PROTEST AND IN CARE, a large-scale group exhibition unfolding bodily complexity and how societal structures disable, O presents solo shows by visual artists Bruno Zhu, Selina Rom Andersen, and Ellinor Åslund. Each exhibition is accompanied by a publication in O’s series, designed by fanfare and released in print and available online for free download. title: Yancey Richardson presents Yale MFA photography graduates in group exhibition
summary: Yancey Richardson is presenting Once More, With Feeling, a group exhibition highlighting the work of the 2026 Yale MFA graduates in photography: Christian Badach, Chen Xiangyun, Jasmine Clarke, Faith Couch, Christopher Postlewaite, Olivia Reavey, John Shen, Em Wall and Andrew Warner. The exhibition is on view from August 12 through August 28, 2026. The Yale MFA in Photography is a celebrated two-year program of study admitting ten students a year. The program is committed to a broad deﬁnition of photography as a lens-based medium open to a variety of expressive means. Students work both individually and in groups with faculty and visiting artists. Christian Badach’s photographs follow the life of a woman named Cedar, who suffers from hypermobility disorder. title: National Sporting Library & Museum extends Nic Fiddian Green retrospective
summary: The National Sporting Library & Museum announced that Nic Fiddian Green: Spiritus Equus, the first-ever retrospective of the acclaimed British sculptor's equine works, has been extended through February 21, 2027. Originally scheduled to close on September 12, 2026, the exhibition will remain on view for several additional months due to popular demand, giving visitors an extended opportunity to experience this landmark presentation. Since 2012, Fiddian Green's monumental sculpture Still Water (2011) has greeted visitors at the entrance to the NSLM's Museum, becoming emblematic of the institution itself. title: MAK exhibition Borderland highlights Ukrainian artist Kateryna Lysovenko
summary: In the MAK exhibition Kateryna Lysovenko: Borderland (16.9.2026–18.10.2026), the Ukrainian-born, Vienna-based artist Kateryna Lysovenko combines the language of classical painting with contemporary issues. In paintings—some of which were created specifically for the MAK—and selected watercolors, Lysovenko juxtaposes vulnerable bodies, hybrid beings, and mythological tales with heroic narratives of war. She investigates the connections between the body and ideology, using the medium of painting to make life in war and exile a tangible experience. With her thematic explorations, she opens up spaces for social and political imagination. Lysovenko views painting as a social act and a political medium. title: Peter Klare blurs the boundaries between painting, photography and sculpture in Berlin exhibition
summary: At Haus am Kleistpark, Peter Klare’s exhibition Schwaananien brings painting, photography and sculpture into close conversation, tracing the ways an image can move off the wall, occupy space and challenge the way viewers understand what they are seeing. On view through September 13, 2026, the exhibition gathers several strands of the Berlin-based artist’s practice, from monumental flower paintings and manipulated photographs to sculptural works made from canvas. Rather than treating these media as separate categories, Klare allows forms, colors and materials to migrate between them, creating a body of work that feels deliberately fluid. At the heart of the exhibition are large-scale floral paintings whose size gives them an almost architectural presence. title: National Gallery of Kosova presents major Xhevdet Xhafa retrospective
summary: The National Gallery of Kosova presents Still Running, a major solo exhibition by Xhevdet Xhafa, one of the pioneering figures of modern art in Kosova. Bringing together works produced over more than six decades, the exhibition traces the continuities and transformations of a practice developed across changing artistic, institutional, and political conditions. Working across painting, drawing, printmaking, performance, assemblage, and relief, Xhafa moves continually between image and object. Everyday things such as shoes, garments, cords, cloth, vessels appear as physical materials incorporated into the work. Attached, folded, covered, or absorbed into dense surfaces, these objects complicate the boundary between representation and material presence. The body remains an insistent presence, even when it is absent. Worn shoes

title: Amanda Levete to deliver the 2026 RSA Metzstein Architecture Discourse
summary: The Royal Scottish Academy announced that internationally acclaimed architect Amanda Levete RA, founder and director of AL_A, will deliver the 2026 RSA Metzstein Architecture Discourse in Edinburgh this September. One of the Academy’s major annual architecture events, the Metzstein Discourse brings leading architects to Scotland to share their ideas and approaches. Amanda Levete RA follows previous speakers including Peter Barber RA OBE, Rafael Moneo, Peter Zumthor, Glenn Murcutt and Grafton Architects. Amanda Levete founded AL_A in 2009, an architecture studio that focuses on creating spaces that promote reciprocity between nature and neighbourhood.
